title: Legislative districts of San Juan

{{Short description|Legislative districts in the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of San Juan''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[San Juan, Metro Manila|San Juan]] in the [[Congress of the Philippines]]. The city is represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the Congress through its [[#Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Manila|Legislative districts of Rizal|Legislative district of San Juan–Mandaluyong}} San Juan, formerly known as San Juan del Monte, was initially represented as part of the [[Manila's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the [[Manila (province)|province of Manila]] in the [[Malolos Congress]] from 1898 to 1899. The then-town was later incorporated to the province of [[Rizal (province)|Rizal]], established in 1901, and was represented as part of the [[Rizal's 1st congressional district|first district]] of Rizal from 1907 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1972. When the then-town was merged to form the [[City of Greater Manila]] during [[World War II]], it was represented as part of the [[Legislative districts of Manila#1943–1944|at-large district]] of Manila from 1943 to 1944. San Juan was separated from Rizal on November 7, 1975 by virtue of Presidential Decree No. 824,{{cite PH act|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/presdecs/pd1975/pd_824_1975.html|chamber=PD|number=824|date=November 7, 1975|access-date=October 10, 2017|title=Creating the Metropolitan Manila and the Metropolitan Manila Commission and for Other Purposes}} and was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] along with other [[Metro Manila|Metropolitan Manila]] municipalities and cities as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV]] from 1978 to 1984. San Juan was grouped with [[Mandaluyong]] from 1984 to 1995 for representation in the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] and the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]], as the [[Legislative district of San Juan–Mandaluyong]]. The two were separated and granted their [https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/hsd/pressrelease/2015_Table%201_Legislative%20Districts.xlsx Legislative districts] psa.gov.ph own representations in Congress by virtue of section 49 of Mandaluyong's city charter (Republic Act No. 7675{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=7675|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_09/RA07675.pdf|date=February 9, 1994 |title=Charter of the City of Mandaluyong |website=www.congress.gov.ph |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303222947/http://www.congress.gov.ph/download/ra_09/RA07675.pdf |archive-date=3 March 2016 |url-status=dead}}) which was approved on February 9, 1994, and ratified on April 10, 1994. ==Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives== {{columns-list|colwidth=10em| {{legend|{{party color|Lakas–CMD}}|[[Lakas–CMD]] (1)|border=1px solid #aaaaaa}} }} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives of [[San Juan, Metro Manila|San Juan]] |- !District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative !
